conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your situation.

First, let me read the official eligibility guidance to make sure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. Now I can help you work out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To start, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have two children - Alex who is 19, and Blake who is 20.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have two children - Alex (19) and Blake (20).

Since both of your children are over 16, an important factor for Child Benefit eligibility is whether they are in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about Alex's situation to be honest - I don't know if they're in any approved education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's okay - we can come back to Alex.

What about Blake? Blake is 20 years old - is Blake currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Blake's actually started an apprenticeship recently - they're doing training in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify something important about Blake's apprenticeship.

According to the eligibility rules I've reviewed, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child "starts an apprenticeship in England."

Since Blake is 20 years old and has started an apprenticeship in England, this would make Blake ineligible for Child Benefit.

Now, going back to Alex who is 19 - you mentioned you're not sure about whether Alex is in approved education or training. Can you tell me:

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex doesn't live with you, another way you could qualify for Child Benefit for Alex is if you're contributing towards their upkeep.

Are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after Alex - for example, for food, clothes, pocket money, or contributing financially to provide them with somewhere to live?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out. I contribute towards Alex's upkeep - things like clothes, food, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

To confirm whether your contributions would qualify you for Child Benefit, I need to understand a bit more:

Are your contributions to Alex's upkeep at least equal to or more than the Child Benefit payment amount (which is currently around £25 per week for the eldest child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute about £26 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful.

Now, going back to the question about Alex's education or training status - even though you're not sure if Alex is in approved education or training, this is quite important for eligibility since Alex is 19.

Child Benefit can only continue for children aged 16-19 if they are in approved education or training. If Alex is not in approved education or training, or if Alex is working 24 hours or more a week (and not in approved education or training), then Alex would not be eligible.

Without knowing whether Alex is in approved education or training, I cannot determine if Alex would be eligible. Do you have any information at all about what Alex is doing - for example, are they working, studying, or something else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I really don't know what Alex is up to at the moment - whether they're working or studying or what. I just don't have that information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. I understand you don't have information about Alex's current situation.

Let me also check a couple more things:

First, do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And just to confirm - is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for either Alex or Blake?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for either of them.

If you're able to find out whether Alex is in approved education or training (or if they're working and how many hours), I'd be able to give you a definitive answer about Alex's eligibility. You could also contact the Child Benefit Office directly with this question.
